clue.text: Poles may be so attractive

definitions.meaning: the ends of a magnet are its north and south poles, so poles have this quality
drawing things or people towards it, as iron is drawn to a lodestone

explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: magnetic poles are the ends of a bar magnet, and a charismatic person is figuratively said to have a pulling power like a lodestone.

clue.text: A large beer, say, for Mrs Masham

indicators.note: the word 'say' signals that the phrase is to be spoken

parts.note: a big ale

explanation.surface: Ordering a pint for a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: Abigail Masham was a favourite of Queen Anne.
explanation.definitionFit: Abigail Masham was lady of the bedchamber to Queen Anne; her first name also came to mean a lady's maid.

clue.text: " A drink divine " from this fruit?

definitions.text: " A drink divine " from this fruit?

parts.words: " A drink divine " from this fruit?
parts.note: the drink of the gods is nectar, so the fruit named after it is suggested as its source

explanation.surface: Asking whether a heavenly drink comes from a particular fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted phrase echoes Ben Jonson's 'the thirst that from the soul doth rise doth ask a drink divine'.
explanation.definitionFit: The smooth-skinned peach takes its name from the drink of the gods.

clue.text: Was first in-also with the sword

indicators.note: the word for 'was first' goes inside the word for 'also'

parts.note: too means also
led means was in front, was first

explanation.surface: Someone was the first to go in, armed with a sword.
explanation.walkthrough: Toledo in Spain was famous for its steel swords, so a Toledo is a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A Toledo is a fine sword blade forged in the Spanish city of that name.

clue.text: By which certain beetles get a jump ahead in America ?

definitions.text: By which certain beetles get a jump ahead in America ?

parts.words: By which certain beetles get a jump ahead in America ?
parts.note: the Colorado beetle is a potato pest; its leaps would be its springs, which is also a city in the USA

explanation.surface: How some insects manage to leap forward in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle file had 4-down's clue on this light; the page prints this one.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in the US state named after the beetle, whose name also suggests the beetles' leaps.

clue.text: Andersen, order a two, wheeler

parts.note: Hans Christian Andersen, the Danish teller of fairy tales
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: An instruction to a Danish storyteller to book himself a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Andersen' stands for his first name, Hans. A hansom is a two-wheeled horse-drawn cab, so 'two-wheeler' is not a bicycle here.
explanation.definitionFit: The hansom cab was a light horse-drawn carriage running on a single pair of wheels.

clue.text: Restrain worker pursued by detective sergeant

indicators.note: the worker comes first and the sergeant follows behind

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker
Sergeant Cuff is the detective in Wilkie Collins's The Moonstone

explanation.surface: Holding back a labourer who is being chased by a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detective sergeant' is not DS but Sergeant Cuff of The Moonstone.
explanation.definitionFit: To handcuff someone is to restrain them with manacles.

clue.text: Some theatre-goers may get their cut from this

definitions.text: Some theatre-goers may get their cut from this

parts.words: Some theatre-goers may get their cut from this
parts.note: the theatre is an operating theatre and the cut is a surgical incision, not a share of the takings

explanation.surface: Audience members receiving their share of the proceeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon's small sharp knife makes incisions on patients in the operating room.

clue.text: Hawthorn's famous vessel ?

definitions.meaning: may is the blossom of the hawthorn tree
the ship that carried the Pilgrim Fathers to America in 1620

explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: hawthorn blossom is called may, and the Pilgrims' ship bore the same name.

clue.text: Scottish law officer is caught in the river

indicators.note: the letters for 'is caught' are placed inside the name of the river

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A Scottish lawman has fallen into a river and is stuck there.
explanation.walkthrough: The procurator fiscal is the public prosecutor in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland the procurator fiscal is the official who investigates deaths and prosecutes crimes.

clue.text: Mermaid ? No, but perhaps its proprietress

definitions.text: Mermaid ? No, but perhaps its proprietress

parts.words: Mermaid ? No, but perhaps its proprietress
parts.note: a mermaid is a lady of the sea, not of the shore; but the Mermaid is also a pub name, and the woman who runs a pub is its keeper

explanation.surface: Is the woman in charge a sea creature? No, but she owns the place.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mermaid was a famous London tavern; the opposite of a sea lady is a lady of the land, which is also the title of a woman running an inn.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who keeps a pub or lets rooms is called by this title, which literally contrasts with a sea-dwelling lady.

clue.text: Rover is such a pilferer

definitions.meaning: a rover is a wandering raider or pirate

explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: a rover in the old sense is a roaming raider, and a plunderer who steals is another word for the same freebooter.

clue.text: Fellow heads the Spanish printers' association

indicators.note: to head is to come in front of, so the word for 'Fellow' goes before the next piece

parts.note: a chap is a man or fellow
el is the Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: A man is president of a trade union for Spanish printers.
explanation.walkthrough: In British printing trades a chapel is the local branch of the union, a meaning the solver may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Printing-house workers traditionally formed a branch of their union known by this church word.

clue.text: Such a man was Antony, and blunt

definitions.meaning: in Julius Caesar Antony calls himself 'a ... blunt man'

explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: Shakespeare's Mark Antony describes himself as an unvarnished, blunt man, and the word also means frank.

clue.text: Abundant outcome, revising futile plan after a loss

indicators.note: revising the phrase rearranges its letters once the A is lost

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A rich result from reworking a useless scheme after a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a loss' says the A of 'a' is taken out of FUTILE PLAN before 'revising' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Plentiful means existing in abundance.

clue.text: Society member's strange associate

parts.note: odd means strange
a fellow is a companion or associate

explanation.surface: A club member's weird companion.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oddfellows are a friendly society, a British mutual-aid organisation; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Independent Order of Oddfellows, a fraternal benefit society, bears this name.

clue.text: Row about one carving-knife victim in car

indicators.note: the line goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a line is a row
I is the Roman numeral one
in Three Blind Mice the farmer's wife cut off the mice's tails with a carving knife, so the creature loses its tail letter

explanation.surface: An argument over a mouse injured by a knife, inside a car.
explanation.walkthrough: The victim is a mouse with its tail cut off, MOUS, from the nursery rhyme Three Blind Mice.
explanation.definitionFit: A limousine is a large luxurious car.

clue.text: Pennon for ship on either side of the river

indicators.note: the ship's letters sit on each side of the river's abbreviation

parts.note: a steamer is a steamship
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A flag for a boat on both banks of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennon is a long narrow flag, and a streamer is a long narrow ribbon or flag.

clue.text: Skill needed to toss priest in a river?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: tossing the priest about mixes up his letters

explanation.surface: What talent does it take to throw a clergyman into a river?
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England; 'toss' makes the priest's letters into PERTIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Expertise is skill or know-how gained by practice.

clue.text: Old writer's aquatic plant

definitions.meaning: the writing material of the ancient Egyptians
a tall sedge growing in the Nile

explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: the ancient writing sheet was made from the Nile reed of the same name.

clue.text: Colour of endless significance to readers

definitions.text: Colour of endless significance to readers

parts.words: Colour of endless significance to readers
parts.note: a yellowish-brown shade that readers know from the title of Kathleen Winsor's 1944 bestseller Forever ..., 'endless' standing for forever

explanation.surface: A colour that means a great deal to people who read books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' is not a deletion signal: it hints at 'Forever', the first word of a famous novel's title.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellowish-orange colour named after fossil resin.

clue.text: Such novel diamonds !

parts.note: Anthony Trollope wrote a novel about a family's jewels, The ... Diamonds

explanation.surface: An exclamation at some remarkably new jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of Lizzie in Trollope's novel about her diamond necklace.

clue.text: Curious escort for a sea-bird

indicators.note: curious means odd, so the letters are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: A strange companion for a gull.
explanation.definitionFit: The scoter is a dark sea duck.

clue.text: Sounds like the circus tent'll overbalance

indicators.note: the clue states openly that what follows is a sound-alike

parts.note: the big top will, contracted to top'll

explanation.surface: Someone warns that the big tent at the circus is going to fall over.
explanation.walkthrough: The circus tent is the big top, so 'the circus tent'll' is 'top'll'.
explanation.definitionFit: To topple is to lose balance and fall over.

clue.text: Access to military engineering lectures

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps
a course is a series of lectures

explanation.surface: Being admitted to classes on army engineering.
explanation.definitionFit: Recourse is a means of access to help, something one can turn to.

clue.text: He deposits his fares at the bank.

definitions.text: He deposits his fares at the bank.

parts.words: He deposits his fares at the bank.
parts.note: sounds like a banker taking in money, but the passengers paying fares are landed on a river bank

explanation.surface: A man pays his takings into a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A boatman who carries passengers across a river sets them down on the far shore.

clue.text: 69 ways of constructing such lays, wrote Kipling

definitions.text: 69 ways of constructing such lays, wrote Kipling

parts.words: 69 ways of constructing such lays, wrote Kipling
parts.note: Kipling's poem In the Neolithic Age says there are nine and sixty ways of constructing lays of this kind, and every single one of them is right

explanation.surface: A literary quotation about how many ways there are to compose songs.
explanation.walkthrough: A lay is a song or ballad; the quotation is from Rudyard Kipling.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling describes songs of the clan or tribe, lays belonging to a people.

clue.text: Switching ends, this sailor would be a rogue

indicators.note: switching means the letters at the two extremities trade places with each other
the ends of the word for a rogue are the letters that change places

parts.note: a rascal is a rogue

explanation.surface: A seaman who, turned round at the edges, would be a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switching ends' swaps the first and last letters of RASCAL, putting L in front and R at the back. A lascar is an East Indian sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Lascars were seamen from India and South-East Asia serving on European ships.

clue.text: Charming fellow corrects errors' about church

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the abbreviation for the church
correcting the errors puts their letters in a different order

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A delightful man puts right mistakes concerning the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charming' here is the magical sense, casting charms; 'corrects' makes SORRER, and 'about' wraps it round the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorcerer casts charms, so he is charming in the magical sense.
